prompt: A week off and no plans. What do you drift towards without deciding to?
helper: The honest answer, not the one that sounds best.

options.label: Fixing or building something physical around the house
A creative project nobody asked for
Getting people together, or starting something
Going deep on a subject until it makes sense

prompt: Which of these could you lose three hours to without noticing?
helper: Think about the last time it actually happened.

options.label: Getting a machine or a system to work properly
Shaping how something looks, sounds or reads
Talking a plan through with someone until it is sharp
Chasing down why something works the way it does

prompt: A project is going badly. What do people turn to you for?
helper: What you are actually asked for, not what you wish you were.

options.label: Making the broken thing work again
A different angle nobody had considered
Holding the group together and keeping it moving
Finding the detail everyone else missed

prompt: What has someone genuinely thanked you for recently?
helper: Real thanks, not politeness.

options.label: Sorting something out with your hands
Making something look or feel right
Listening properly when it mattered
Catching a mistake before it cost anything

prompt: Something has stopped working and nobody knows why. What do you do first?
helper: Your actual first move, not the textbook one.

options.label: Start testing parts until I find the one at fault
Step back and look for a completely different approach
Ask whoever was closest to it what changed
Work through it methodically from the start

prompt: You are stuck on something hard. What gets you unstuck?
helper: What has actually worked before.

options.label: Trying things until something gives
Leaving it and letting an idea arrive sideways
Explaining it out loud to somebody
Reading until I understand it properly

prompt: How true is this: a blank page excites me more than a finished draft to fix.
helper: There is no better answer here — both are real ways to work.

options.label: Completely true — I want the blank page
Mostly true
Mostly false — I would rather improve something real
Completely false — give me the draft

prompt: Would you rather invent the idea, or be the one who makes it actually work?
helper: Both are needed. Which is you?

options.label: Invent it — the idea is the interesting part
Lean towards inventing
Lean towards making it work
Make it work — an idea nobody shipped is nothing

prompt: You have to give bad news to someone who will not like it. How does that sit?
helper: Everyone finds it uncomfortable. The question is what you do with it.

options.label: I would rather write it than say it
I would find the words that land gently
I would say it straight and deal with the reaction
I would rather someone else did it

prompt: In a meeting where you disagree with everyone, what happens?
helper: Be honest about the room, not the ideal version of yourself.

options.label: I keep it to myself and write it up after
I ask questions until they see it themselves
I say it plainly and argue for it
I look for the version everyone can live with

prompt: A tool you need has no tutorial, only documentation. What happens next?
helper: This is about appetite, not ability.

options.label: Good — I would rather read the source of truth
I would get through it if I needed to
I would find a person to show me instead
I would look for a tool that does not need it

prompt: How do you feel about work where the tools change every couple of years?
helper: Some people find that energising and some find it exhausting.

options.label: That is the appeal
Fine, as long as the point of the work stays put
I would rather get deep in one craft
I would rather the ground stayed still

prompt: A small shop is doing well. What do you find yourself wondering?
helper: Whatever your mind actually goes to first.

options.label: What their margins look like
How I would grow it
Whether the people working there are happy
Honestly, none of that crosses my mind

prompt: Would you rather own a share of the outcome, or be paid reliably for the work?
helper: Neither is wrong. They lead to different places.

options.label: A share of the outcome, with the risk that carries
Mostly the outcome
Mostly the reliable pay
Reliable pay — I want to think about the work, not the risk

prompt: Picture the room you work best in. What is it like?
helper: Where you actually do good work, not where you think you should.

options.label: A workshop or site — somewhere things happen
Quiet, mine, nobody interrupting
A studio with other people making things
Wherever the people are — a desk is incidental

prompt: Which would wear you down fastest?
helper: The thing you could not do for years.

options.label: Sitting still at a screen all day
Constant meetings and interruptions
Work with no room to make it your own
Working alone with nobody to talk to

prompt: A new skill you need for work. How do you actually pick it up?
helper: The way that has worked, not the way you admire.

options.label: Doing it badly until I am doing it well
Understanding the theory first, then applying it
Watching somebody good and copying them
A structured course with a clear order

prompt: You have one month to get good enough at something to be useful. What is your plan?
helper: Whatever you would genuinely do.

options.label: Build something real with it immediately
Find the best explanation and work through it
Find someone doing it and ask to shadow them
Make a schedule and work through it in order

prompt: Which would make you feel the work had been worth it?
helper: The one you would actually be proud of.

options.label: Something I built is still being used
Something I made moved somebody
People are better off because I was there
I built something that stands on its own

prompt: Twenty years in, what would you want said about your work?
helper: Not the most impressive answer — the one you would want.

options.label: It worked, and it kept working
Nobody else would have made it that way
They looked after people properly
They saw it before anyone else did
